title: The limits of erasure-based postselection for quantum error mitigation
summary: In both classical and quantum error correction, heralded erasures are known to be easier to tolerate than unheralded general stochastic errors. Whilst an established benefit of loss-dominant quantum architectures such as photonic qubits, this fact has received renewed interest, with a pivot towards reconstructing other architectures to be erasure-dominant, such as dual-rail transmons.
